contexts.text: The land shall not be cut off in the famine () = lest man should perish through a lack of truth... To be cut off = to perish.
To cut off the frogs from thee, and from thy houses () = that reasonings may cease... To cut off = to cease; for to cut off is predicated of the frogs, and to cease of the reasonings.
To cut off from it man and beast () = to vastate good interiorly and exteriorly. AE 386:9. AE 388:20.

Thou wouldst be cut off from the earth () = that so there would no longer be any communication by means of the things of the Church. To be cut off, when said of the things of the Church, = to be separated; and when they are separated, or when there is no longer any communication with Heaven by means of the things of the Church, that man then falls into Hell, which is to be cut off.

That soul shall be cut off from Israel () = that he will be separated from those who belong to the Spiritual Church, and will be damned. To be cut off = to be separated, and also to be damned. AC 7907.
Shall be cut off from his peoples () = separation and spiritual death. To be cut off and killed = to be separated from those who are in good and thence in truths; and to perish as to spiritual life.
He shall be cut off from his peoples () = separation from Heaven and the Church, and spiritual death. To be cut off from peoples = separation and spiritual death: it = separation from Heaven.

That soul shall be cut off from the midst of his peoples () = that Heaven and the Church is not with him, but Hell. To be cut off from the midst of his peoples = separation from the Church, and spiritual death; thus that the Church is not with him, but Hell. Explained.
His groves ye shall cut down () = that their doctrinal things are to be utterly rejected.

For the name [not] to be cut off and destroyed before Jehovah () = the quality of the state through which conjunction is effected; which state is the spiritual state of those who belong to the Church.
I will cut off the Cherethites ().
To cut off man from the surfaces of the land () = [to cut off] the affection of truth and wisdom.
That the falsities of evil are to be destroyed, is signified by the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and shall fall to the earth (). AE 391:29.

That then there will be nothing of the Church left among the Jews, is described by I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the war bow shall be cut off (), by which is signified that there will no longer be any truth in doctrine, nor understanding of truth, and consequently no combat and resistance against falsity. AE 357. AE 734:5.
Under Cast down, see this reference.

For three years he had not found any fruit on the fig-tree, and he therefore told the vine-dresser to cut it down (), by which is signified that from beginning to end there had been no natural good with that nation.

To ascend to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Lebanon, and to cut down the loftiness of his cedars, and the choice of his fir-trees () = the endeavour to destroy the goods and truths of the Church, both internal and external. AE 654:14.
To cut off the little child from the street, and the youth from the broad places () = the vastation of truth nascent, and of truth born.
He will cut off from Israel head and tail () = that all the intelligence and knowledge of truth will perish from them. AE 624:16.
That the defence of truth against falsity will become none, is signified by all the men of war shall be cut off ().
That this falsity is destructive of all the good of the Word and of the Church, is signified by I will set My faces against that man, and will cut him off from the midst of his people ().
I will cut off from Babel the name and the residue ().
Lest ye be cut off on account of her iniquity ().
